note: quelque chose = something; autre chose = something else; pas grand-chose = not much.
l'homme can mean mankind/humans in general.
jour = day as a unit/date; journée = the day as a span of time (toute la journée).
One word for time AND weather: Quel temps fait-il ? = What's the weather like? Also grammatical tense.
ex: Je n'ai pas le temps. — I don't have time.

note: ma femme = my wife; there is no separate everyday word for 'wife'.
Counted 'time' (once, twice): une fois, deux fois, la première fois. Never temps here.
ex: Deux fois par semaine. — Twice a week.

note: se serrer la main = to shake hands; à la main = by hand.
Plural is completely different: un œil, des yeux. coup d'œil = glance.
Quelle heure est-il ? = What time is it? à l'heure = on time.
ex: Il est trois heures. — It's three o'clock.

note: tout le monde = everybody; il y a du monde = it's crowded.
ex: Tout le monde est là. — Everyone is here.

note: an for counting (trois ans, j'ai 20 ans); année for the year as a span (toute l'année, une bonne année).

faux: ≠ infant only — a child of any age

note: ma fille = my daughter; une fille = a girl (jeune fille = young woman).
faire la tête = to sulk; en tête = in the lead.
Bonne nuit ! = Good night! (when going to bed).
coup de téléphone = phone call; coup d'œil = glance; tout à coup = suddenly; du coup = so, as a result.
ex: Donne-moi un coup de main. — Give me a hand.

note: Capitalised Dieu = God; mon Dieu ! = my God!
à la maison = at home; fait maison = homemade.
avoir l'air (+ adj) = to look, seem.
ex: Tu as l'air fatigué. — You look tired.

note: soir = evening as a point in time (ce soir); soirée = the whole evening, or a party.
en ce moment = at the moment, currently.
petit ami / petite amie = boyfriend / girlfriend; mon ami can imply a partner.
Plural messieurs (mes + sieurs). Used as polite address: Bonjour, monsieur.
avoir besoin de = to need (the usual way to say 'need').
ex: J'ai besoin d'aide. — I need help.

note: Always plural: les gens. For a counted number use personnes: trois personnes.
nom (de famille) = surname; prénom = first name.
la mort = death; le mort / la morte = dead man / woman.
d'accord = OK, agreed; être d'accord = to agree.
ex: Je suis d'accord. — I agree.

note: avoir peur (de) = to be afraid (of); faire peur à = to frighten.
ex: J'ai peur du noir. — I'm afraid of the dark.

note: à côté (de) = next to, nearby; de côté = aside; du côté de = towards, near.
ex: Il habite à côté. — He lives next door.

note: mot = a single word; parole = spoken words, speech, lyrics.
avoir raison = to be right; avoir tort = to be wrong.
ex: Tu as raison. — You're right.

note: une place = seat or town square; de la place = room/space. A 'place' in general is often endroit or lieu.
en fait = actually, in fact; au fait = by the way.
par terre = on the floor/ground; la Terre = the Earth.
poser une question = to ask a question; il est question de = it's about.
Final -ps silent: [kɔʁ]. Same form in singular and plural.
ex: Le corps humain. — The human body.

note: Pronounced [fis] (s sounded, l silent); ≠ fil (thread), whose plural fils is pronounced [fil].
dans la rue = in the street.
One word for both story and history; also 'fuss': Pas d'histoires ! = No fuss!
Also a railway carriage.
Everyday meaning is money (uncountable: de l'argent); also the metal silver.
The normal word for a human face (face is mostly 'side, front').
Room in general = pièce; salle = hall/room for a purpose.
à pied = on foot.
année = the year as a span (toute l'année, bonne année); an for counting (trois ans).
matin = point in time (ce matin); matinée = the whole morning.
travaux (pl.) = construction work, roadworks.
ex: Je cherche du travail. — I'm looking for work.

note: en ville = in town, downtown.
les affaires = business, or one's belongings; une bonne affaire = a bargain.
faux: rarely a love affair — mainly matter, case, deal
ex: C'est mon affaire. — That's my business.

note: par cœur = by heart; avoir mal au cœur = to feel sick.
à part = apart from; de la part de = on behalf of; quelque part = somewhere.
ex: C'est de la part de qui ? — Who's calling?

note: Used until evening (then bonsoir); dire bonjour = to say hello.
ex: Bonjour, madame ! — Hello, madam!

note: Masculine despite the -e: un problème.
à peine = hardly; ce n'est pas la peine = no need; ça vaut la peine = it's worth it.
ex: Ce n'est pas la peine. — There's no need.

note: tout de suite = right away; par la suite = later; à la suite de = following.
ex: J'arrive tout de suite. — I'm coming right away.

note: à point = medium (steak); sur le point de = about to.
être en train de + infinitive = to be (doing) right now.
ex: Je suis en train de manger. — I'm eating right now.

note: Un instant ! = Just a moment!; pour l'instant = for now.
à la fin = in the end; en fin de compte = ultimately; fin (adj.) = thin, fine.
au bout de = at the end of / after (time); un bout de pain = a bit of bread.
ex: Au bout de la rue. — At the end of the street.

note: aller au lit = to go to bed.
du nouveau = something new; la nouvelle = (piece of) news or short story.
ex: Il y a du nouveau ? — Anything new?

note: Colloquially un type = a guy.
garçon for a waiter is dated; say serveur.
Plural mesdames (mes + dames). Polite address for any adult woman.
de toute façon = anyway; de cette façon = this way.
ex: De toute façon, c'est trop tard. — Anyway, it's too late.

note: le tour = turn, tour, trick, circumference; la tour = tower (la tour Eiffel).
ex: C'est ton tour. — It's your turn.

note: À table ! = Dinner's ready!
en tout cas = in any case; au cas où = just in case; dans ce cas = in that case.
ex: En tout cas, merci. — In any case, thanks.

note: avoir de la chance = to be lucky; Bonne chance ! = Good luck!
ex: Tu as de la chance ! — You're lucky!

note: à force de = by dint of, through repeated.
au fond = basically / at the back; à fond = thoroughly; ≠ fonds (funds).
ex: Au fond de la salle. — At the back of the room.

note: le livre = book; la livre = pound (sterling, or 500 g).

ex: Un regard triste. — A sad look.

note: avoir envie de = to feel like, want.
faux: mainly = desire, wish; envy is secondary
ex: J'ai envie d'un café. — I feel like a coffee.

en: fire; traffic light; light (for a cigarette)
note: feu rouge = red light; Tu as du feu ? = Got a light?; au feu ! = fire!
Informal; very common for 'thing' when the word escapes you.
sans doute = probably (!); sans aucun doute = without a doubt.
ex: Il viendra sans doute. — He'll probably come.

note: en route = on the way; Bonne route ! = Safe trip!
Order = command/sequence; ordering in a shop or restaurant is commande.
avoir lieu = to take place; au lieu de = instead of.
ex: La fête aura lieu samedi. — The party will take place on Saturday.

note: Plural cieux = heavens (literary/religious); ciels in technical/painting use.
pays = country (nation); the countryside is la campagne.
Masculine despite -ence: le silence.
une pièce = a room (of a home), a coin, a (theatre) play, or a piece/part.
en quelque sorte = in a way; de sorte que = so that.
avec plaisir = gladly; faire plaisir à qn = to please sb.
à cause de = because of.
ex: À cause de la pluie. — Because of the rain.

note: A cook is chef only in a restaurant (chef de cuisine).
faux: ≠ just a cook — any boss or leader
ex: Mon chef est en vacances. — My boss is on holiday.

note: prendre un verre = to have a drink; homophones: vert (green), vers (towards), ver (worm).
faire partie de = to be part of; a celebration is une fête / une soirée.
ex: Une partie de cartes. — A game of cards.

note: Slang.
en face (de) = opposite; face à = facing. A person's face is visage.
faux: a person's face is visage, not face

note: Usually plural: les cheveux = hair. Body/animal hair = poil.
du reste = besides; les restes = leftovers.
ex: Le reste du temps. — The rest of the time.

note: Colloquial filler genre = 'like'.
avoir de l'esprit = to be witty; venir à l'esprit = to come to mind.
avoir le droit de = to be allowed to; le droit = law (as a field of study).
Quel âge as-tu ? = How old are you?
se rendre compte = to realise; tenir compte de = to take into account.
Homophones: mère (mother), maire (mayor).
l'État = the State (government); en bon état = in good condition.
jeu de cartes = pack of cards; jeux vidéo = video games.
en général = generally, usually.
la police = the force; a police officer = un policier.
chemin de fer = railway; en chemin = on the way.
The usual word for 'a place' (un bel endroit); à l'endroit = right side out.
The whole day: toute la journée; Bonne journée ! = Have a nice day!
Informal; pronounced [ga] (r and s silent).
Vulgar; extremely common as an interjection of anger or surprise.
